name: Solenne Atelier Vantablack Devotion Robe
description:
A floor-length ceremonial robe by Solenne Atelier's spiritual commission line, constructed in collaboration with the Church of the Signal Unbroken. The outer layer is Vantablack-treated silk-analog — a material so light-absorbent that the wearer appears to be a hole in space. Inner lining is hand-embroidered with gold-thread circuit diagrams representing the BCI neural communion ritual. The hood is structured to frame neural port hardware as crown-like adornment.

Each robe is commissioned individually. No two embroidery patterns are identical — the circuit maps reflect the wearer's personal neural signature.
functionality: BCI port framing in the hood collar displays neural hardware as intentional ornamentation. Thermal underlining regulates temperature during long ceremonies. Hem is weighted for controlled movement during ritual procession.
what_it_says: This person has wealth, faith, and the conviction to merge both into a single visible statement.
worn_by: Church of the Signal Unbroken clergy
story_hooks: The neural signature embroidered into a deceased cleric's robe contains an encrypted data fragment — someone needs it extracted without the Church knowing.
A counterfeit version has appeared on the Shelf, worn by someone claiming spiritual authority they don't have.
The Vantablack treatment is sourced from a single Shelf-based chemist who has just been disappeared.
